description: Run several MiraStudio tools in order, in one call. Use it when the steps are already decided and none of them needs a decision based on the previous one — building a scene, posing a whole limb, spawning and placing a set of props. It saves turns, not milliseconds: each step still costs the same inside Studio. **There is no rollback.** Every step is validated up front (unknown method, malformed step, nesting, screenshot) and the batch is refused as a whole if any step is unusable, but once execution starts a failing step stops the batch and leaves the earlier ones applied — Studio's undo stack has no notion of a transaction, and several tools clear it outright. So the result is always returned, never an error: read 'ok', and on failure 'stopped_at' and 'error' tell you exactly how far it got. Prefer the multi-entry tools (studio_set_character_bone, studio_set_character_ik) over a batch of single writes: they apply as one undo step, a batch does not.

steps.description: the calls to run, in order. Any MiraStudio tool except studio_screenshot (its image would come back as unusable base64 text) and studio_execute_batch itself

params.description: that tool's arguments; omit for a tool that takes none

executed.description: how many steps ran; on failure this is also the index of the step that failed

stopped_at.description: index of the failing step, null when 'ok'

error.description: why the batch stopped; the steps before it are applied and stay applied

code.description: same codes as a direct call: -32602 invalid params, -32000 studio not ready, -32001 operation failed, -32002 timeout, -32003 not found

steps.description: one entry per step that ran, in order

result.description: exactly what the tool would have returned on its own
